concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper-bound notation for growth rates of running times.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Formal sums of coefficient multiples of powers of a variable, with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi with real a, b, including modulus, conjugation and the exponential e^{iθ}.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, each head moving at most one cell per step.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.name: Linear maps and matrix rank
concepts.gloss: Matrices represent linear maps between vector spaces, and the rank of a matrix is the dimension of its image.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Tensor products
concepts.gloss: The tensor product of vector spaces or operators builds a multi-index space or acts independently on each index; the paper's label space and simultaneous butterfly layers are tensor products.

evidence.quote: The ambient label space is $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$ with its tensor bilinear form.

concepts.name: Nondegenerate bilinear forms
concepts.gloss: A bilinear form pairs vectors into scalars; it is nondegenerate when no nonzero vector is orthogonal to everything, which lets a subspace split off its orthogonal complement.

evidence.quote: This form has eigenvalues $1$ and $1-h/9=-91/9$, so it is nondegenerate.

concepts.name: n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen's conjecture that n-bit integer multiplication needs order n log n time, here read as an eventual Ω(n lg n) lower bound for every fixed multitape machine.

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth
The theorem refutes an eventual $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound for every fixed multiplication machine in this model.

concepts.title: $n\log n$ optimality conjecture

symbols.name: input bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

symbols.name: logarithm
symbols.meaning: The logarithm function, so n log n is the conjectured optimal growth rate.

concepts.name: Harvey–van der Hoeven multiplier
concepts.gloss: The previously established deterministic multitape algorithm multiplying N-bit integers in O(N log N) time, used here only as an ordinary subroutine on short records.

evidence.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper bound
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine calls; they do not invoke the improved theorem recursively.

concepts.name: Arrays on tape and elementary stream operations
concepts.gloss: Multi-index arrays are stored in lexicographic address order with implicit addresses, and fixed digit permutations, digit moves, splits into streams and merges each cost O(V) for logical bit volume V.

evidence.quote: An array with address set $[a_1]\times\cdots\times[a_t]$ is stored in lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant.
The \emph{logical volume} $V$ is the number of stored data bits.

concepts.name: Controlled shifts
concepts.gloss: Linear-time updates that add to, or cyclically shift, a later address field by an amount computed from earlier fields, possible because the target field follows its control fields in tape order.

evidence.quote: The next operations are linear because their target field follows their control fields.

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product of polynomials modulo x^S − 1 (or its multidimensional analogue), where exponents wrap around cyclically.

evidence.quote: Here $*$ denotes cyclic convolution on the product of the coordinate groups and a dot denotes coordinatewise multiplication.

concepts.name: Multiplication as digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Splitting each integer into radix-2^b digits turns their product into the convolution of short digit sequences, followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Normalized discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The map sending a length-q vector to the averages of its entries multiplied by powers of a q-th root of unity; it is a contraction and diagonalizes cyclic convolution.

evidence.quote: Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction, since each output averages inputs multiplied by complex numbers of modulus one.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: An algebra isomorphism x ↦ ∏ x_i^{μ_i} that turns a cyclic convolution of length S = ∏ s_i into a multidimensional cyclic convolution on pairwise coprime axes, implemented by triangular controlled shifts.

evidence.quote: First, the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution.

concepts.name: Fixed-point approximation and error accounting
concepts.gloss: Complex values are stored on the grid 2^{-p}(ℤ+iℤ) in the unit disk, truncated toward zero, and errors of approximate contractions add when composed.

evidence.quote: For any array, let $Q_p$ truncate each real and imaginary coefficient part toward zero to this grid.
Composing such algorithms adds their errors

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey and van der Hoeven's identity expressing a Fourier transform of coprime length s through one of a nearby length t, using Gaussian-weighted contractions, so prime-length axes become power-of-two axes.

evidence.quote: Our starting point is the Gaussian-resampling reduction of Harvey and van der Hoeven
Gaussian resampling connects these two shapes.

concepts.name: Retained transform permutations
concepts.gloss: Instead of sorting, the source and target coordinate permutations of resampling stay inside the transform identity; the target one is absorbed by the chirp and the source one cancels across forward transforms, pointwise product and inverse transform.

evidence.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula and compute that formula directly.
Finally, the source permutation retained during resampling cancels across the two forward source transforms, their pointwise product, and the opposite-sign transform.

concepts.name: Bluestein's chirp identity
concepts.gloss: A Fourier transform equals pointwise multiplication by a quadratic-phase chirp, a cyclic convolution with the chirp, and another chirp multiplication.

evidence.quote: Next, Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring ℂ[y]/(yʳ+1)
concepts.gloss: The ring of complex polynomials of degree below r with y^r = −1, in which multiplying by a power of y is a signed shift of the coefficient list and powers of y act as roots of unity.

evidence.quote: one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two.
Multiplication by $y^a$, for any integer $a$, permutes the coefficients and changes some signs

concepts.title: Polynomial ring $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$

symbols.name: complex numbers
symbols.meaning: The field of complex numbers from which the coefficients are taken.

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The polynomial indeterminate, whose r-th power equals −1 in the ring.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.name: Coefficient phase twist
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k with ζ = e^{πi/r} maps cyclic convolution modulo x^r − 1 isomorphically onto negacyclic multiplication modulo y^r + 1.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$; its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic wrap after the twist is removed.

concepts.name: Normalized butterfly H₀
concepts.gloss: The two-point map H₀(u,v) = ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2), the radix-two step of fast Fourier-type transforms, applied coefficientwise to polynomial records.

evidence.quote: the transform calculation consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations.

concepts.title: Normalized butterfly $H_0$

symbols.name: normalized butterfly
symbols.meaning: The two-point linear map sending (u,v) to ((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2).

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadic numbers
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are rationals with power-of-two denominators, the ring ℤ[i,1/2], in which the butterfly layers are computed exactly.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics, whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: Nussbaumer's Fourier transform over ℂ[y]/(y^r+1) using powers of y as roots of unity, so it needs only signed shifts, butterflies and address rearrangements, with a stored frequency order consumed by the inverse transform.

evidence.quote: These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and Nussbaumer
Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes, and multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list.

concepts.name: Signed Kronecker packing
concepts.gloss: Packing the signed fixed-point coefficients of two ring elements into large integers so one call to the O(N log N) multiplier yields their exact polynomial product.

evidence.quote: The reduction is a signed form of Kronecker substitution
Their polynomial products use signed packing and the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier as an ordinary subroutine.

concepts.name: Linear network with wire roles
concepts.gloss: A fixed finite circuit of linear gates on wires, each wire's fixed place called its role, which in three stages exchanges two data banks (X,Y) ↦ (−Y,X) with prescribed signs.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary value.
A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.

concepts.name: Restoration of scratch values
concepts.gloss: A gate schedule that subtracts the effect of arbitrary initial auxiliary values, performs the update, and undoes its copies so every scratch wire ends with its initial value.

evidence.quote: We call all these auxiliary wires \emph{scratch wires}; their initial values may be arbitrary.
This cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation

concepts.name: Three-element subset construction
concepts.gloss: Data indexed by 3-element subsets of a 100-set are combined by gather/scatter through central wires, giving coefficients depending on intersection size, and side wires cancel the unwanted ones so the net effect is y ← y + x.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.

concepts.name: Frames and the common-frame identity
concepts.gloss: Each network vertex gets an invertible operator D_v on the wire's array; edges apply D_v D_u^{-1}, pointwise gates commute with a common frame, so the whole network implements D_out S D_in^{-1} on rows split cyclically among the roles.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.
Distribute rows cyclically among the $W$ roles, padding the row count for each prefix to a multiple of $W$.

concepts.name: Subspace labels and orthogonal residuals
concepts.gloss: Nested nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed m-dimensional bilinear space are attached to the network's vertices, and the dimension of the orthogonal residual on each edge counts the smaller operations needed there.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space.
Their dimension changes count the smaller operations needed on an edge

concepts.name: Rank saving s < Wm
concepts.gloss: The key finite fact: the total number s of smaller calls over all edges of a network with W wires and label dimension m is strictly less than Wm.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.title: Rank saving $s<Wm$

symbols.name: smaller call count
symbols.meaning: The total number of smaller recursive calls, the sum of edge ranks or residual dimensions over all network edges.

symbols.name: wire count
symbols.meaning: The number of wires (roles) in the finite network, including scratch wires.

symbols.name: label dimension
symbols.meaning: The dimension of the ambient label space, equal to the number of sub-fields a parameter is split into per recursion level.

concepts.name: Recursive power saving
concepts.gloss: Splitting the work into s calls each on volume V/W gives the normalized recurrence F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k−1} + O(1), and s/W < m^τ with τ < 1 yields cost O(V e^τ) instead of O(V e).

evidence.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$.
This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Address shear
concepts.gloss: The address permutation (H,D) ↦ (H+D,D) on two field groups, which together with two linear-cost updates gives the interchange (H,D) ↦ (D,H).

evidence.quote: For the bit procedure, that endpoint operator is an address shear

concepts.name: Lower triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Every rational matrix of rank a factors as E₁ΠE₂ with invertible lower triangular E₁, E₂ and a partial permutation Π with a ones, a reordered Bruhat factorization.

evidence.quote: The required factorization is the Bruhat factorization for arbitrary matrices, with coordinate order reversed

concepts.name: Rational matrix interface
concepts.gloss: The XOR bit network with projection matrices as frames, whose endpoint differences are the identity on every role, so it implements the address shear with total edge rank s_b < W_b m.

evidence.quote: For a nondegenerate rational subspace $U\subset\mathcal F$, write $P_U$ for the projection onto $U$ along $U^\perp$.
The bit network has $W_{\rm b}$ wires, uses only pointwise XOR gates

concepts.name: Fast address-chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: The first tape procedure: exchanging two disjoint u-bit address fields of an array in O(V u^τ) time with τ < 1, by recursively running the bit network with shears as edge frames.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits in an array whose addresses form a complete Cartesian product.
Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

concepts.name: Binary phase interface
concepts.gloss: The complex network over Gaussian dyadics with binary labels, whose edge frames are products of two-point kernels C = HSH and whose endpoints telescope to a tensor power of C, convertible to the H₀ layer.

evidence.quote: Its phase-frame difference $\mathcal C_V\mathcal C_U^{-1}$ is a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$, or its inverse, per vector in an orthonormal basis of the edge residual.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: Changing selected address bits in several chunks at once by whole-chunk cyclic shifts and moves, followed by a deterministic repair of an explicitly bounded set of exceptional addresses.

evidence.quote: We implement a binary row addition on corresponding selected bits in two address chunks.
Those changes are implemented by whole-chunk moves and controlled shifts, followed by a deterministic correction of the explicitly identified exceptional addresses.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: The second tape procedure: applying H₀ at the same bit position of up to d address chunks at once in O(V d^{λ'}) time with λ' < 1, computed exactly in Gaussian dyadics and truncated once.

evidence.quote: one selects the same bit position in each of at most $d$ equal-width address chunks, and the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a fixed $\lambda'<1$.
A single truncation follows the completed contractive layer.

concepts.name: Convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: Normalized cyclic convolution of arrays over ℂ[y]/(y^r+1) computed by two forward synthetic transforms on a tape layout using chunk interchanges and simultaneous layers, packed pointwise products, and the opposite transform.

evidence.quote: The two forward synthetic transforms retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product, and the opposite transform consumes that order.

concepts.name: Exact recovery by rounding and carries
concepts.gloss: Removing known scales, bounding the coefficient error strictly below 1/2, rounding to integers and propagating carries gives the exact binary product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product.

concepts.name: Parameter choice and cost balance
concepts.gloss: Fixed rational exponents (τ, λ′, c, ε, δ, …) and sizes d ≈ p^ε, K ≈ d^c make every normalized cost-table term at most p^{1−2κ}, with smallest margin 2^{−181} = 2κ.

evidence.quote: A compatible choice of rational parameters makes all terms in its cost table fit Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n(lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.gloss: A single deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine computes the exact product of two n-bit integers in O(n(lg n)^{1−κ}) worst-case time with κ = 2^{−182}, refuting the n log n lower-bound conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers
The algorithm is exact for every input length and disproves the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture of Sch

concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: big-O
symbols.meaning: Asymptotic upper bound up to a constant factor.

symbols.name: input bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

symbols.name: ceiling binary logarithm
symbols.meaning: The binary logarithm rounded up, and at least 1.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^{−182} by which the logarithmic factor's exponent drops below one.
